objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: Use the preterite for a bounded completed event. Regular -ar endings are -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. Nosotros -amos looks like the present; a time expression such as ayer establishes the past.
commonMistakes: Compré and compró distinguish yo and él/ella/usted. Neither is interchangeable with present compro.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: In the yo preterite, -car changes c to qu before é and -gar adds u before é: busqué, pagué, llegué. This preserves sound. Other persons keep the ordinary stem in these verbs.
commonMistakes: Do not spread the yo spelling change to tú: buscaste, not busquaste.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Lo/la/los/las can replace an explicitly identified direct object. Agree with that object and place the pronoun before a conjugated verb. This lesson uses things to avoid regional variation in pronouns for people.
commonMistakes: Do not match the pronoun to the buyer. It replaces the item bought.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

stimuli.SpanishText: Ayer visité la tienda con Ana. Busqué una camisa azul, pero compré una verde. La compré porque me gusta el color. Ana compró zapatos negros y los pagó con su dinero. Yo pagué veinte euros por la camisa. Llegué a casa a las seis y guardé la ropa en mi cuarto. Mi madre preguntó por la camisa. Yo hablé de la tienda cerca del parque.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.
